The company’s long-term trajectory is stagnant, with compounded profit growth over the last decade at a meager 4% [E17], and the trailing twelve months show a catastrophic profit decline of -421% [E19]. Furthermore, the business has struggled to generate top-line momentum, delivering poor sales growth of -19.2% over the past five years [E55]. Investors are also denied any immediate return on capital, as the dividend yield is 0.00% [E3]. The bear’s focus on long-term profit stagnation [E17] and historical sales declines [E55] ignores the critical inflection point currently underway, as evidenced by the explosive 450% YoY sales growth [E58] and strong recent momentum [E59, E60]. While the bear highlights the trailing twelve-month profit volatility [E19], it fails to account for the accelerating earnings growth [E61] that suggests a fundamental turnaround is already in progress. However, the company’s ROA of -9.37% significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of -171.35% [E7], indicating that the business is managing its asset base far more efficiently than its peers during this recovery phase. Furthermore, the market is clearly pricing in this operational improvement, as evidenced by the stock trading at a P/B of 2.63x, which remains a discount to the sector benchmark of 3.77x [E6]. By fixating on past data, the bear overlooks the clear evidence of a structural shift in performance that justifies the current market optimism [E50].

The bull’s reliance on recent sales spikes [E58, E59, E60] ignores the reality that the company has suffered from poor sales growth of -19.2% over the past five years [E55], suggesting these recent figures may be volatile outliers rather than a structural shift. While the bull claims a turnaround is in progress, the trailing twelve-month profit growth of -421% [E19] and a 10-year compounded profit growth of only 4% [E17] demonstrate a long-term inability to generate sustainable earnings. However, this relative efficiency is undermined by an ROE of 0% [E8] and a complete lack of shareholder returns via dividends [E3]. The current market optimism is disconnected from financial reality, as evidenced by the fact that price growth is currently outpacing profit growth by 715% [E50]. Relying on a P/B of 2.63x [E6] to justify valuation is misleading when the company fails to produce meaningful profit growth [E17, E19] or consistent returns [E8].
